CAREER LEVEL
Entry-level
ESG Analyst / Sustainability Associate / ESG Reporting Associate
An Environmental, Social and Governance (ESG) Associate helps organisations measure, report, and improve their environmental and social impact, ethical practices, and corporate governance.

ESG professionals may work on carbon emissions, energy consumption, waste management, employee welfare, supply-chain responsibility, business ethics, sustainability reporting, and climate-related risks.

A degree in Environmental Studies & Sustainability provides a foundation in environmental systems, climate change, resource management, and sustainable development. Students can complement this knowledge with corporate reporting, data analysis, business fundamentals, and ESG frameworks.
The role is relevant to graduates interested in connecting environmental responsibility with business performance, investment decisions, and organisational accountability.

Career progression
Job titles and responsibilities vary. Some positions focus on environmental data, while others concentrate on reporting, responsible investment, social impact, or governance.
Year 1
Foundation
Understand sustainability fundamentals

items.text: Study environmental science, climate change, biodiversity, and natural resource management.
Understand sustainable development, circular economy, and environmental justice.
Learn introductory economics, business concepts, and corporate responsibility.
Build spreadsheet and data-visualisation skills.
Follow sustainability reports from companies and public institutions.
Practise writing short reports on environmental and social challenges.

blocks.text: Year 2
Core skills
Learn ESG frameworks and measurement

items.text: Understand environmental, social, and governance indicators.
Study sustainability reporting and materiality assessment.
Learn the fundamentals of greenhouse-gas accounting, including Scopes 1, 2, and 3.
Explore the Global Reporting Initiative (GRI), IFRS Sustainability Disclosure Standards, and relevant Indian reporting requirements.
Practise data collection, validation, calculations, and documentation.
Learn basic Power BI or Tableau for sustainability dashboards.

blocks.text: Year 3
Application
Build an ESG portfolio

items.text: Prepare a mock ESG assessment of a company using publicly available information.
Calculate example emissions using transparent assumptions and appropriate emission factors.
Compare sustainability indicators across two or three organisations.
Study supplier screening, stakeholder engagement, and ESG risk assessment.
Seek internships in sustainability consulting, corporate ESG teams, environmental research, or responsible investment.
Produce a concise ESG report or dashboard with evidence and limitations.

blocks.text: Year 4
If applicable
Prepare for ESG recruitment

items.text: Complete a capstone project on climate risk, sustainability reporting, or social impact.
Practise materiality assessments and ESG data-quality checks.
Learn to explain sustainability findings to finance, operations, and management teams.
Prepare a portfolio with reports, calculations, dashboards, and recommendations.
Apply for ESG analyst, sustainability associate, and reporting roles.
Consider postgraduate study if it supports your chosen specialisation.

blocks.text: Adapt this roadmap to the duration and curriculum of the selected programme. A three-year degree can cover the same competencies on a compressed schedule.
A. Environmental and Climate ESG
Measures emissions, energy use, water consumption, waste, climate exposure, and environmental performance.

blocks.label: Key skills
blocks.text: Carbon accounting, environmental indicators, climate-risk basics, data analysis.

blocks.label: Potential roles
blocks.text: Climate Analyst, Environmental ESG Analyst, Carbon Accounting Associate.
B. ESG Reporting and Disclosure
Collects, validates, and presents sustainability information for corporate disclosures and reporting frameworks.

blocks.label: Key skills
blocks.text: Reporting standards, documentation, data validation, spreadsheet analysis.

blocks.label: Potential roles
blocks.text: ESG Reporting Associate, Sustainability Reporting Analyst, Disclosure Analyst.
C. Social Impact and Responsible Supply Chains
Assesses labour practices, employee welfare, human rights, community impact, diversity, and supplier responsibility.

blocks.label: Key skills
blocks.text: Stakeholder engagement, social-impact measurement, supplier assessments, research.

blocks.label: Potential roles
blocks.text: Social Impact Analyst, Responsible Sourcing Associate, Sustainability Programme Associate.
D. Governance and ESG Risk
Supports the evaluation of business ethics, board oversight, compliance processes, risk exposure, and governance practices.

blocks.label: Key skills
blocks.text: Risk assessment, policy review, due diligence, documentation, analytical reasoning.

blocks.label: Potential roles
blocks.text: ESG Risk Analyst, Governance Research Associate, Sustainability Due Diligence Analyst.
E. Sustainable Finance and Responsible Investment
Evaluates how sustainability risks and opportunities relate to investment analysis, lending, and financial decision-making.

blocks.label: Key skills
blocks.text: Financial literacy, ESG indicators, investment research, climate-risk analysis.

blocks.label: Potential roles
blocks.text: ESG Investment Analyst, Sustainable Finance Associate, ESG Research Analyst.

rows.text: Climate change, resources, biodiversity, circular economy

blocks.text: Data analysis and reporting
Excel or Google Sheets for emissions calculations, indicator tracking, data validation, and sustainability reporting tables.
Dashboards and visualisation
Power BI or Tableau to communicate trends in emissions, energy, water, safety, or social indicators.
Standards and guidance
Explore the Global Reporting Initiative, the IFRS Foundation's sustainability disclosure standards, and relevant guidance from the Greenhouse Gas Protocol.
Company and environmental data
Review corporate sustainability reports, annual reports, official environmental statistics, and publicly available emissions or energy data. Record source dates, boundaries, and assumptions.
You do not need to master every ESG framework at the beginning. Start with Excel, sustainability reporting fundamentals, carbon accounting concepts, and one dashboard tool.
Complete at least three projects that demonstrate your ability to analyse sustainability information and communicate findings.

blocks.label: Project 1
blocks.text: ESG performance assessment

blocks.label: Focus
blocks.text: ESG reporting
Select a company with publicly available sustainability disclosures. Review its environmental, social, and governance indicators and compare them with its stated targets.

blocks.label: Deliverables
blocks.text: ESG indicator table, evidence sources, reporting gaps, peer comparison, and improvement recommendations.

blocks.label: Project 2
blocks.text: Greenhouse-gas emissions inventory

blocks.label: Focus
blocks.text: Carbon accounting
Build a sample inventory using clearly identified activity data and appropriate emission factors. Categorise relevant sources under Scope 1, Scope 2, and selected Scope 3 categories.

blocks.label: Deliverables
blocks.text: Calculation workbook, data-source register, assumptions, emissions summary, and data-quality limitations.

blocks.label: Project 3
blocks.text: Sustainability dashboard

blocks.label: Focus
blocks.text: ESG analytics
Use a public or clearly labelled sample dataset to track energy use, water consumption, waste, emissions, or workforce indicators over time.

blocks.label: Deliverables
blocks.text: Interactive dashboard, indicator definitions, trend analysis, and recommendations for management.
For each project, document the data sources, measurement boundaries, methodology, assumptions, limitations, and findings. Do not present estimated or sample data as verified company performance.

How to improve your chances

items.text: Learn the fundamentals of ESG reporting and sustainability indicators.
Build a sample emissions workbook and a sustainability dashboard.
Read actual sustainability reports and practise identifying gaps in evidence or disclosure.
Highlight analytical writing, spreadsheet skills, and environmental knowledge on your CV.
Apply to ESG reporting, sustainability operations, climate research, and related entry-level roles.

rows.text: GRI Standards and IFRS Sustainability Disclosure Standards
Greenhouse Gas Protocol and Scope 1, 2, and 3 concepts
Excel, Power BI or Tableau, data validation
Physical and transition risks, climate scenarios
Governance, human rights, supply-chain due diligence

blocks.text: Choose reputable training providers and verify whether a certification is recognised by employers in your target market. For entry-level jobs, a strong applied portfolio may be more useful than accumulating multiple introductory certificates.
Postgraduate study is optional for many associate roles but can support technical or specialised ESG careers.
Master's in Environmental Management or Sustainability
Suitable for environmental performance, sustainability strategy, resource management, and corporate sustainability.
Master's in Climate Science, Climate Policy, or Environmental Science
Useful for climate-risk analysis, carbon management, environmental assessment, and climate-policy work. Check quantitative and science prerequisites.
MBA in Sustainability or Master's in Sustainable Finance
Appropriate for ESG strategy, sustainable investment, business transformation, and corporate sustainability leadership.
Master's in Public Policy or Environmental Policy
Suitable for environmental regulation, sustainability policy, public-sector programmes, and climate governance.

Integrate sustainability into organisational priorities and decision-making

blocks.text: Progression depends on the employer, technical specialisation, and experience. Senior roles may require substantial business, regulatory, or technical expertise.
ESG professionals may increasingly work on:

blocks.label: Climate-risk assessment
blocks.text: Understanding physical climate risks and the financial implications of transition policies.

blocks.label: Carbon accounting and decarbonisation
blocks.text: Measuring emissions and evaluating reduction strategies.

blocks.label: Sustainability reporting
blocks.text: Improving disclosure quality, traceability, and consistency.

blocks.label: Supply-chain responsibility
blocks.text: Assessing environmental and human-rights risks across suppliers.

blocks.label: Sustainable finance
blocks.text: Integrating sustainability risks into investment and lending decisions.

blocks.label: Nature and biodiversity
blocks.text: Assessing dependencies and impacts on ecosystems and natural resources.

blocks.label: ESG data and assurance readiness
blocks.text: Improving data controls, documentation, and verification processes.
Reporting rules and employer requirements change across jurisdictions, so professionals should monitor the standards and regulations relevant to their work.
Use this checklist to assess readiness for entry-level ESG roles.
ESG readiness tracker
I understand environmental, social, and governance factors.
I can explain the basics of sustainability reporting frameworks.
I understand Scope 1, Scope 2, and Scope 3 emissions.
I can use Excel or Google Sheets to organise and validate data.
I can create a sustainability dashboard or clear data visualisation.
I can review a corporate sustainability report and identify evidence gaps.
I have completed at least two ESG or sustainability projects.
I can document assumptions, sources, and methodological limitations.
I have tailored my CV and applications for ESG or sustainability roles.
Check off each item as you build the competency. This is a preparation guide, not a hiring guarantee.
By graduation, a strong candidate should be able to:

items.text: Explain key environmental, social, and governance concepts.
Collect, organise, and validate sustainability data.
Understand core ESG reporting frameworks and carbon accounting principles.
Prepare clear reports, charts, and dashboards.
Identify sustainability risks and propose practical improvement opportunities.
Demonstrate analytical and communication skills through projects or internships.

blocks.label: Recommended starting point
blocks.text: Learn Excel, ESG reporting fundamentals, and greenhouse-gas accounting. Then complete a company ESG assessment and a sample sustainability dashboard to demonstrate your readiness for ESG Associate, ESG Analyst, or Sustainability Reporting Associate roles.
